sections.html:
Shelbyville is Bedford County's seat, and a sale here involves both a county office and a city office. Mid-2025 estimates show 26,146 residents, up 11.1% since 2020 and well above the 20,335 counted in 2010.

The typical owner-occupied house is valued at $244,000, and owners live in only 50.7% of occupied homes. Renters pay a median $1,056. Because 28.4% of residents are under 18, family houses with several bedrooms sell steadily, and with half the housing rented, small investor-owned properties turn over regularly.

sections.h2: Bedford County rates after the 2026 reappraisal
sections.html:
Bedford County was in a reappraisal year, and most owners received higher appraisals. On June 30, 2026 the county commission approved its budgets and kept the property tax at the state's certified rate. The old rate of $2.3252 for every $100 assessed dropped to the certified $1.5083, so the average owner should see little change in the bill unless a value rose faster than the county average.

Bedford County 2026 rates by fund
County fundRate per $100 assessed
County General Fund$0.9276
General Purpose Schools$0.4022
General Debt Service$0.0973
Highway and Public Works$0.0584
County Capital Projects$0.0228
Total county rate$1.5083

Residential parcels are assessed at one quarter of appraised value. The city levies its own tax on top.

sections.h2: Does a lower rate mean a lower bill?
sections.html:
No, not by itself. Following a reappraisal the state certifies a rate meant to bring in about the same total from existing property, and a rate above it is treated as a tax increase for most owners. Your own bill can still change if your appraisal moved faster or slower than the county average, or if you built something new.

Check with the Assessor of Property on the value in your parcel record, and on whether a newer garage or deck is included. Expect a buyer's agent to look at the same record.

The city takes payment for its levy separately from the county. Options: a third-party processor online or by phone (it adds a fee), a mailed check to the City of Shelbyville, P.O. Box 185, Shelbyville, TN 37162, or the counter at City Hall, 201 North Spring Street on the Public Square. A mailed check should carry the top stub and the receipt number.

Ask the city for the current-year city rate, since the county announcement covers only the county portion. The current year's bill is due the first Monday of October, and the previous year's stays interest-free until February 28. Two governments bill on their own, so the title company should pull both statements ahead of closing.

sections.h2: Tax relief for older or disabled owners
sections.html:
Bedford County's freeze income cap is $43,780 for 2026, compared with the statewide floor of $38,470. Applications close 35 days after the delinquency date, which lands in April. Separate programs serve disabled former service members and low-income elderly or disabled owners.

The freeze holds the bill at what it was in the first approved year, so mention it to the buyer's side if the house has one. On a larger lot, ask the assessor about greenbelt classification, which has a March 15 application deadline.

Building and Codes, (931) 488-4230, wants a permit before you build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or tear down a structure, and before pools, decks, arbors or storage buildings go in. Permits now run only through the city's OpenGov portal, and some residential, fence, sign, accessory structure and driveway applications are online only. The department enforces the 2018 International Codes, and simple permits can be issued the same day.

A buyer who wants different zoning goes through the Planning Department, a pre-planning meeting, the Planning Commission and two City Council readings, and the ordinance takes effect 15 days after the public hearing. A sale usually needs no rezoning, but confirm the current zone before you promise a buyer a use such as a duplex or a home business.

  • Phone first for any repair that touches structure or systems.
  • Keep permit finals with your closing documents.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Bedford County
sections.html:
Bedford County's Register of Deeds records ownership, liens and contracts for public notice, and sends the state's conveyance and mortgage taxes to the Department of Revenue monthly. An online fee calculator covers any filing, and a free fraud alert service tells you when a transfer is recorded under your name. State law puts 37 cents on every $100 of sale price, plus 11.5 cents per $100 of mortgage debt beyond the first $2,000.

The title company usually files the deed, and your contract decides who pays the tax.

Rain and snow add up to about 59.4 inches across roughly 128 days a year here, so inspectors tend to press on roofs, crawl spaces and drainage. School attendance zones are set by Bedford County School District, which can confirm any address a buyer asks about.

Owners live in barely half of occupied homes, so a tenant already in place is common. Have the lease, the rent and the end date ready before you discuss price. Investors compare your ask with the $1,056 median rent, and anyone wanting a vacant house needs the move-out date.

• The county statement and the city statement.
  • Your deed, plus a list of mortgage or lien balances.
  • Permit finals for decks, additions or other work.
  • Proof of any freeze or greenbelt status on the parcel.
  • Lease details for any tenant.

A title company can order most of it, yet having it in hand when an offer arrives can save days, and it lets a cash buyer give you a firm number sooner.

1. You describe the house, any tenants and any open permits.
  2. A buyer sends an offer, and you accept it in writing.
  3. The title company orders the county and city tax statements and checks for liens.
  4. Any balance owed on taxes or a mortgage is paid from the sale proceeds.
  5. You sign the deed, and it is recorded with the Bedford County Register of Deeds.

With a cash buyer there is no lender review, so the closing date follows title work and your own schedule.

A standard listing puts the most eyes on the house. A cash buyer who takes it with tenants in place or repairs undone can close as fast as title work allows.

Weigh a cash figure against what a listing would leave after commission, repairs and holding costs. Get the offer in writing, clear the county and city tax statements and let a title company record the deed.

faqs.q: What is the Bedford County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: On June 30, 2026 the commission set the state's certified rate of $1.5083, which replaces last year's $2.3252. The city bills its own tax separately.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Shelbyville city property tax?
faqs.a: At City Hall, 201 North Spring Street, by mail to P.O. Box 185, online, or by phone at 1-866-414-2699. Online and phone payments carry a third-party fee.

faqs.q: Can I get a permit for a fence or accessory building?
faqs.a: Yes, through the city's OpenGov portal. Fence, accessory structure, sign and driveway applications are online only. Call (931) 488-4230 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax on a Shelbyville sale?
faqs.a: The state takes 37 cents per $100 of price, collected at recording. Your contract says which side pays it.

faqs.q: What is the freeze income limit for Bedford County?
faqs.a: $43,780 for tax year 2026. Applicants must be 65 or older and meet the program's ownership and residence rules.
